items.readable_text:
Content:
We can write down a geometric series in a compact way using the sigma notation
[MATH: S = \displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^N a_1r^{n-1},]
where [MATH: a_1] is the first term of the series, [MATH: r] is the common ratio, and [MATH: N] is the number of terms in the series.

Content:
For instance, suppose we wish to write the following geometric series in sigma notation:
[MATH: S= 2+4+8+16+32+64+128]

Content:
In this case, [MATH: a_1 = 2] and [MATH: N = 7.] To find [MATH: r,] we calculate the ratio of the first two terms in the series:
[MATH: r = \dfrac{a_2}{a_1} = \dfrac{4}{2} = 2]

Content:
Therefore, expressing the geometric series given in sigma notation, we obtain
[MATH: 2+4+8+16+32+64+128 = \sum_{n=1}^{7} 2\cdot 2^{n-1}.]

Content:
Finally, we can simplify the above series using the laws of exponents, as follows:

Content:
[MATH: ∑_(n = 1)^(7)2 ⋅ 2^{n − 1}|= ∑_(n = 1)^(7)2 ⋅ 2^{n} ⋅ 2^{− 1}; = ∑_(n = 1)^(7)2 ⋅ 2^{n} ⋅ (1)/(2); = ∑_(n = 1)^(7)2 ⋅ (1)/(2) ⋅ 2^{n}; = ∑_(n = 1)^(7)2^{n}]

sections.normalized_html:
We must express the given series in the form [MATH: \sum_{n=1}^{N}a_1 r^{n-1},]

where [MATH: a_1] denotes the first term of the series, [MATH: r] denotes the common ratio, and [MATH: N] denotes the number of terms in the series. In this case, [MATH: a_1 = 1.]

To find [MATH: r,] we find the ratio of the consecutive terms [MATH: a_1] and [MATH: a_2 \mathbin{:}] [MATH: r = \dfrac{a_2}{a_1} = \dfrac{3}{1} = 3]

Now we must determine [MATH: N] (the index of the last term). To do this, we use the fact that [MATH: a_N = a_1 \cdot r^{N - 1} .]

Therefore, [MATH: a_{N}|= a_{1} ⋅ r^{N − 1}; 243|= 1 ⋅ 3^{N − 1}; 3^{5}|= 3^{N − 1}; 5|= N − 1; N|= 6.]

Expressing the geometric series in sigma notation, we obtain

[MATH: 1 + 3 + 9 + ⋯ + 243|= ∑_(n = 1)^(6)1 ⋅ 3^{n − 1}; = ∑_(n = 1)^(6)3^{n − 1}.]
